source_text: Quam vehementer inculcat apud iustum iudicem Deum aliena peccata aliis non nocere, qui commendans mortem Christi vigilanter enuntiat propter nostra illum delicta, quae et plura erant et nostra erant, non propter unum et alienum et olim defuncti hominis mortem oppetiisse?
pass_a_gloss: How vehemently he stamps in that with a just judge God another's sins do not harm others, who, commending the death of Christ, vigilantly enunciates that he met death on account of our offenses, which both were more and were ours, not on account of one and another's and of a human being long dead?

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: How forcefully he impresses upon us that, before God the just judge, one person’s sins do not harm others! Praising Christ’s death, he carefully declares that Christ underwent death because of our offenses—which were both many and ours—not because of one offense belonging to another, a man long dead (Romans 4:25).

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
